lines.text: This is your token board book. Four laminated pages are bound on the left, with a tab for each: Choices, Targets, Board, and Tokens.
lines.screen: The closed book lies on a table with its four labelled tabs showing on the right, then it opens to the first page.

lines.text: Page one is the Choices page. Show it before the task begins. Every picture should be something your learner values right now, not something they can get any time, or have just had plenty of.
lines.screen: The Choices page fills the frame, with six choice cards on its six boxes.

lines.text: Your learner looks over the pictures and picks one to work for. If needed, help with the pointing, but let your learner make the choice.
lines.screen: The learner's small hand moves across the cards, points at one, then pinches it and lifts it off the page.

lines.text: Page two is the Targets page, where you choose what to teach: a new skill, or a replacement behavior from the behavior plan. If the target is asking for something, like a break, still give what was asked for, every time.
lines.screen: The page turns to the Targets page, with six teaching target cards on its boxes.

lines.text: Choose one target at a time. Agree with the other adults on exactly what counts, so everyone gives tokens for the same thing.
lines.screen: The teacher's hand, with a shirt cuff, picks the target card and lifts it off the page.

lines.text: Page three is the Board. Place the target under First, and the chosen item under Then. Your learner can now see the plan: first the target, then the item.
lines.screen: The page turns to the Board; the target card goes into the First box and the chosen item card into the Then box, and each box glows as the plan is named.

lines.text: Page four is the Tokens page, where the tokens wait. The empty slots on the board show your learner how many are left to earn. Make new tokens valuable first; the tips at the end show how.
lines.screen: The Tokens page appears beside the Board with its tokens in their boxes, and the empty token slots on the Board are highlighted.

lines.text: Before you start, decide how much of the target behavior earns a token: how many times, or how long. Keep it small, so your learner can succeed. This example uses one token for every two minutes.
lines.screen: A note over the Board and Tokens page reads: one token for every two minutes of the target behavior.

lines.text: Now start the session. Point to the board and name both pictures: first the target, then the item. The ring counts down each two-minute interval, sped up for this video.
lines.screen: The teacher's hand points to the First card, then the Then card; a timer ring labelled as sped up appears beside the Board and counts down from 2:00.

lines.text: The interval is over, and your learner kept up the target behavior the whole time. Give a token right away, with brief praise that names what they did. Let your learner put it in the next slot.
lines.screen: As the ring completes, the teacher's hand takes a token from the Tokens page at once and holds it out with a speech bubble of praise that names the target; the learner's hand puts it in the first slot, which glows.

lines.text: If the behavior stops, there is no token for that interval, but the earned tokens stay on the board. Calmly remind your learner what to do right away, and start the interval over when they begin again.
lines.screen: The ring stops part way and turns grey; a note says no token this interval and the earned tokens stay; the teacher's hand points to the target at once, and a fresh 2:00 interval starts.

lines.text: Each interval with the target behavior earns another token, given right away with a few words of praise. The board fills up, one slot at a time.
lines.screen: The intervals run faster now; token after token goes into the next slot, each with a short bubble of praise.

lines.text: One more interval earns the last token. It looks different: this is the terminal token, earned just like the others. With practice, it tells your learner that the board is finished and the item comes next.
lines.screen: After one more interval the teacher's hand holds out the last token, with its own picture and an orange double border; the learner's hand puts it in the last slot, which carries an orange ring.

lines.text: One more interval with the target behavior, and the last token goes in. Now the board is full, and your learner has earned the item they chose.
lines.screen: After one more interval the last token goes into the last slot, and every slot on the Board is full.

lines.text: The board is full, so trade the tokens for the Then item right away, especially while the board is new. Your learner gets it for the time or amount set before the session.
lines.screen: The teacher's hand gathers the tokens off the board back to the Tokens page; the Then card lifts and grows into the item, and the teacher's hand passes it to the learner's hand, which takes it away.

lines.text: When the time with the item is up, put it away, and return the pictures to their pages. Then your learner chooses again for the next round.
lines.screen: The teacher's hand brings the item back and it shrinks into its card; the hand returns the target card to the Targets page and the chosen card to the Choices page, and the learner's hand points over the choices again.

lines.text: Three tips. Make the tokens valuable first: give one and trade it for the item right away, again and again, until your learner reaches for the token. Start with a small requirement and few tokens, and raise them slowly; if the behavior falls apart, go back a step. Keep the item available only through the board.
lines.screen: Three short tips appear one by one beside the book: make the tokens valuable first, start small and raise slowly, the item only through the board.

lines.text: That's the whole cycle: choose, set the target, earn the tokens, and exchange. Over time, the target behavior should happen more often; if not, change the item or the requirement. The back of each page tells you more.
lines.screen: The book closes on the table with its four tabs showing, and the four steps of the cycle appear one by one.

lines.text: This is a token board for the bus ride. It rides along with your learner, and the bus staff use it the same way on every trip.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: Across the top are your learner's own bus rules, each with a picture, so everyone can see what earns a token. Two to four rules work best.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: Before the ride, your learner picks something to work for, and it goes in the Earn box, so the goal is in sight the whole way.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: This is the route, drawn simply, from the start of the ride to the stop. The form takes the usual length of the ride, which you can check in Maps.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: The form spreads the tokens over the ride. It divides the time by the number of tokens, so the last token comes a minute or two before the stop, just as your learner gets close to the item.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: Here the tokens come at a set interval, such as every few minutes. On a long ride the board can fill more than once, with an exchange each time it is full.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: To start, the bus staff use a timer set to the checkpoint times on the plan. A vibrating watch is easy to use on a noisy bus. The timer here is sped up for this video.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: At each checkpoint, if your learner followed the rules since the last one, give a token right away, with brief praise that names the rule. Let your learner put it on the board.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: If a rule is not followed, that checkpoint earns no token, but the earned tokens stay. Calmly name the rule once, and the next checkpoint is a fresh chance.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: With a row for each rule, every rule earns its own token at each checkpoint. A missed rule leaves only its own slot empty, and the other rules still earn.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: The bus rolls on, and each checkpoint with the rules followed earns another token. The board fills up along the way.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: The last token comes just before the stop. The board is full, and your learner has earned the item.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: When the last slot is filled, the board is full, and your learner has earned the item. On a long ride, the board then starts again.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: At the stop, the board goes with your learner to the adult who meets the bus. That adult sees the full board and gives the item right away.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: When the board is full, your learner gets the item right there on the bus. Something small and quick works best. Check the district’s rules before using food on the bus.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: Once the board is working, fade the timer. Use landmarks along the route as the checkpoints instead: places your learner can see from the window, in the order the bus passes them.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: Then use fewer checkpoints: every other landmark, and later just the stop. If the rides get harder, go back a step.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: The form prints a ride plan for the bus staff, with the route, the checkpoints, what to say, and a log to fill in after each ride.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).

lines.text: Same board, same rules, every ride. Over time, the rides should go more smoothly, with fewer tokens needed.
lines.screen: The bus ride walkthrough (a bus book, v21.49).
